title: Beat sync re-enables manually disabled scheduled tasks
reasoning: The function explicitly documents that it should not re-enable entries manually disabled in Django admin, but update_or_create always applies defaults containing enabled=True for existing rows. Any beat restart will therefore turn disabled code-managed PeriodicTask rows back on, causing intentionally paused scheduled jobs to resume.
reproduction: Create a PeriodicTask with a name from app.conf.beat_schedule and enabled=False, then trigger sync_beat_schedule_to_db; update_or_create writes enabled=True back to the row.
recommendation: For existing PeriodicTask rows, preserve the current enabled value. For new rows, default enabled=True. This can be done by get_or_create followed by selective field updates that exclude enabled for existing records, or by reading the existing enabled value into defaults before update_or_create.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests only provide settings overrides and do not exercise django-celery-beat synchronization behavior or the documented disabled-task contract.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test with django_celery_beat installed that creates a disabled PeriodicTask matching a beat_schedule entry, runs sync_beat_schedule_to_db, and asserts it remains disabled.
minimumFixScope: Change sync_beat_schedule_to_db in bahk/celery.py to preserve enabled on existing PeriodicTask records.
